Objective
\n

To be hired by someone under 35 and never, ever bring it up.

\n

I have 29 years of shipping software and I'd like to spend the next few doing exactly that, quietly, without anyone having to hear how it used to be done. It used to be done worse. There. That's the last you'll hear of it. I'm not asking for a title with \"Distinguished\" in it. I'm asking for a laptop, a ticket, and about forty-eight hours before you notice the ticket is closed. What follows is a legally binding list of the things I will not do, say, or visibly think, as a condition of employment.

\n
\n\n
\n
The Pledge
\n

I solemnly swear I will not:

\n
    \n
  1. 01Say \"well, in my day.\" My day is today. I checked. It's on the calendar you invited me to and then rescheduled four times.
    2. \n
  2. 02Explain what a modem sounded like, what a floppy disk was for, or why the save icon looks like that. You've seen the memes. We're good.
    3. \n
  3. 03Point out that the thing you just invented had a different name in 2004 and shipped on a CD. I'll write it in a notebook. The notebook stays home.
    4. \n
  4. 04Say \"we tried that.\" Even if we did. Even if it went pear-shaped in a way that is still, frankly, hilarious.
    5. \n
  5. 05Have opinions about tabs, spaces, microservices, or your framework out loud. I will have them. I'll scream them into a pillow like a professional.
    6. \n
  6. 06Post \"Thrilled to announce\" about anything. I do not rise at 4am. I do not have a morning routine. I have coffee, and I am not publicly grateful for it.
    7. \n
  7. 07Reference Fight Club more than once a quarter. First rule, et cetera.
    8. \n
  8. 08Reply-all. Ever. I've seen things. I've been things.
    9. \n
  9. 09Mention that I wrote a computer science book that sold 30,000 copies, or that my podcast was the number one tech podcast, or that I was a public face of a Microsoft product. None of that is relevant and I would never bring it up. See above, where I didn't.
    10. \n
  10. 10Start a sentence with \"kids these days.\" Several of the kids are my boss now, and they're doing fine. Mostly. I'd love to help with the parts that aren't. Quietly. From a desk. That you give me.
    11. \n

Experience
\n

All of it real. Lightly seasoned.

\n
CTO, Red:4 Aerospace · Big Machine, Kōlea2025 to now
\n

\"Independent,\" which is what unemployment is called once it has a Stripe account. Built Kōlea, a complete newsletter and sales platform, alone, end to end. A 24-year-old founder would call that \"a lean team with 10x leverage\" and raise on it. I call it a Tuesday. It has a slop meter that catches machine-sounding writing, which I'm told is \"not a moat.\" It works, though. Things I build tend to.
